skills.name: Similar figures and the scale factor

note.text:
Similar figures have the same shape: corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are in the same ratio.
• The scale factor (constant of proportionality) k = a side of the image ÷ the corresponding side of the object.
• Every length of the image = k × the matching length of the object.
• Two triangles with equal angles are always similar.
• All squares, all circles and all equilateral triangles are similar; rectangles in general are not.
Shadows: at the same time of day, heights are proportional to shadow lengths.

sections.heading: Same shape, different size
sections.text:
A photo printed small and large shows the same picture: the shape is the same, only the size changes. Such figures are similar.
In similar figures:
• corresponding angles are equal;
• corresponding sides are in the same ratio.
That common ratio is the scale factor k (also called the constant of proportionality).

sections.heading: Finding lengths
sections.text:
Find k from one pair of matching sides: k = side in the image ÷ matching side in the object.
If a {4} cm side becomes {6} cm, k = {6} ÷ {4} = {1.5}. Then a {10} cm side becomes {1.5} × {10} = {15} cm.
Match short with short and long with long. If k is less than {1}, the image is smaller.

sections.heading: Shadows and heights
sections.text:
At the same moment, the sun's rays hit all objects at the same angle. A pole and a tree with their shadows form similar right-angled triangles.
If a {2} m pole has a {3} m shadow and a tree has a {15} m shadow, the scale factor is {5}, so the tree is {5} × {2} = {10} m tall.

key_words.meaning: same shape: equal angles, sides in the same ratio

examples: k = {3}: a {2} cm side becomes {6} cm

mistake.wrong: A {4} cm by {6} cm rectangle grows to {8} cm by {10} cm (add {4})
mistake.why: Similar figures are enlarged by multiplying, not by adding the same amount.

worked_example.problem: Two similar triangles: a side of {a} cm in the small one matches {b} cm in the large one. Another side of the small triangle is {c} cm. Find the matching side of the large one.
steps: Large side = {b / a} × {c} = {b / a * c} cm.

cards.idea: Scale factor k = image side ÷ matching object side.
Multiply every length by k to get the matching length.
example: k = {4}: a {5} cm side becomes {20} cm.

cards.idea: Similar means the same shape: equal angles, sides in the same ratio.
example: All circles are similar; not all rectangles are.

pick.q: Which pair of figures is always similar?
e: A long thin rectangle is not the same shape as a square-like one.
Isosceles triangles can have different angles.
Right-angled triangles can have different other angles.
pick.y: Every circle is an enlargement of every other circle.

pick.q: Which pair of figures is always similar?
e: Parallelograms can have different angles and side ratios.
pick.y: All angles are 90° and all sides are equal: squares differ only in size.

pick.q: Two triangles have angles 50°, 60°, 70° and 70°, 50°, 60°. They are…
w: similar only if they are right-angled
e: Equal angles do not fix the size.
Equal angles always make triangles similar.
Any triangles with equal angles are similar.

questions.prompt: A side of {a} cm in one figure matches a side of {a * k} cm in a similar, larger figure. What is the scale factor?

misconceptions.explain: The scale factor multiplies: divide, do not subtract.
Divide the larger by the smaller to enlarge: {a * k} ÷ {a}.

questions.prompt: Triangle PQR is similar to triangle ABC with scale factor {k}. AB = {x} cm. Find PQ.

misconceptions.explain: Scale factors multiply lengths, they do not add to them.

questions.prompt: Two similar rectangles: the small one is {a} cm by {b} cm. The long side of the large one is {c} cm. Find its short side.

misconceptions.explain: Similar figures are in proportion: multiply by the scale factor, do not add the difference.
Match short with short and long with long.

questions.prompt: At {X.t}, a {h} m pole in Bamenda casts a shadow {s} m long. At the same time a tree casts a shadow {s * m} m long. How tall is the tree (m)?

misconceptions.explain: Height ÷ shadow is the same for both: tree = {h} ÷ {s} × {s * m}.
Use the ratio, not the difference.

solution: The sun's rays make similar triangles: height ÷ shadow is the same.
